title: System integrations
seoTitle: API, SQL & Business System Integration | EFIops
metaDescription: Connect business applications, APIs and databases. EFIops builds focused integrations for data exchange, reporting and more dependable workflows.
h1: Close the gaps between your systems.
lead: When one system finishes, another person shouldn’t have to start copying. Connect the records your applications, reports and workflows need—with validation, ownership and somewhere for failed transfers to go.

sections.heading: The gap between two systems becomes somebody's job.
paragraphs: Orders arrive in one place. Reporting needs them somewhere else. Machine exports have a different format. Another spreadsheet joins it all together.
We examine the handoff: what data is needed, which system is responsible for it and what should happen when a transfer is delayed or incomplete.

sections.heading: Useful connections, with clear ownership.
items: API integrations. Exchange suitable information between applications and supported services.
Database connections. Provide controlled access to the records a report or application needs.
Data preparation pipelines. Consolidate exports, normalise formats and prepare records for analysis.
Event and workflow connections. Connect an agreed change in one system to the next step in another.
Integration repairs. Investigate mismatched records, failed transfers and repetitive manual fixes.

sections.heading: Build for the transfer and the exception.
paragraphs: We agree the source of truth, the mapping and the direction of each connection. The implementation includes appropriate validation, error handling and a way to identify failed work.
Testing covers missing values, repeated requests, format changes and interrupted transfers. The handover explains what is connected and how the integration is monitored.

faqs.question: Do both systems need an API?
faqs.answer: An API is often useful, but some projects work with database access or structured exports. We review the options and their limitations first.

faqs.question: Can you combine machine exports for reporting?
faqs.answer: Yes. Industrial data processing is part of Karol's experience. The source format and required output define the scope.

faqs.question: Will this replace our existing systems?
faqs.answer: The first question is whether they can be connected effectively. A focused integration may be enough to improve the handoff.

faqs.question: What happens if a provider changes its API?
faqs.answer: Integrations need maintenance. Monitoring and support can be scoped so failures are visible and changes can be addressed.

cta.label: Discuss your systems
cta.heading: Where are people moving the same information twice?
cta.text: Tell us which systems are involved, which records need to move and what currently happens between them.

primaryIntent: business system integration; API integration developer; SQL integration.
summary: Move information between APIs, databases and applications with fewer manual handoffs.

useCases.title: A form shouldn’t need retyping.
useCases.body: Map the useful details into the right record, track the transfer and make incomplete requests visible.

useCases.title: Use the same order in both places.
useCases.body: Connect the source of truth to reporting, keeping identifiers and definitions consistent across the handoff.

useCases.title: Different format. Same useful record.
useCases.body: Normalise agreed files and fields, handle repeats, and hold incomplete rows for review instead of silently dropping them.
